# Use a standard Ubuntu base image for broad compatibility
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# To run MPI as root in a container, this environment variable is often needed.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Install all necessary dependencies in a single layer to optimize image size.
# This includes build tools, git, cmake, OpenMPI for parallel execution,
# FFTW library, ca-certificates, and libgomp1.
# FIX: Added python3, which is a required dependency for the LAMMPS cmake build system.
RUN apt-get update && \
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    git \
    cmake \
    build-essential \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libfftw3-dev \
    python3 \
    libgomp1 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# This single RUN command performs all steps to download, build, and install LAMMPS.
# Chaining these commands together and cleaning up in the same layer significantly
# reduces the final Docker image size.
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git /lammps_src && \
    mkdir -p /lammps_src/build && \
    cd /lammps_src/build && \
    # Configure the LAMMPS build using CMake.
    # -D BUILD_MPI=yes: Enables MPI support.
    # -D PKG_REAXFF=yes: Enables the ReaxFF package as requested.
    # -D PKG_KSPACE=yes: Includes FFT-based solvers, common for many simulations.
    # -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local: Ensures binaries are installed to a standard PATH location.
    cmake ../cmake \
      -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
      -D PKG_REAXFF=yes \
      -D PKG_KSPACE=yes \
      -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local && \
    # Build LAMMPS using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Install the 'lmp' executable to /usr/local/bin, which is on the system PATH.
    # This fulfills the requirement to copy the executable to a system location.
    make install && \
    # Create the final working directory.
    mkdir /app && \
    # Copy the specified example files into the working directory.
    cp /lammps_src/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /app/ && \
    # Clean up the source code and build artifacts to minimize the final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /lammps_src

# Set the final working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /app

# The 'lmp' executable is now on the PATH.
# When running in a containerized environment (like Kubernetes), you may need to add
# specific flags to mpirun for compatibility, e.g.:
# mpirun --mca btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism none -np <cores> lmp -in <input_script>
# Setting a default command to the lammps executable.
CMD ["lmp"]

    cmake \
    build-essential \

RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git /lammps_src && \
    mkdir -p /lammps_src/build && \
    cd /lammps_src/build && \
    # Configure the LAMMPS build using CMake.
    # -D BUILD_MPI=yes: Enables MPI support.
    # -D PKG_REAXFF=yes: Enables the ReaxFF package as requested.
    # -D PKG_KSPACE=yes: Includes FFT-based solvers, common for many simulations.
    # -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local: Ensures binaries are installed to a standard PATH location.
    cmake ../cmake \
      -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
      -D PKG_REAXFF=yes \
      -D PKG_KSPACE=yes \
      -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local && \
    # Build LAMMPS using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Install the 'lmp' executable to /usr/local/bin, making it available on the system PATH.
    make install && \
    # Create the final working directory.
    mkdir /app && \
    # Copy the specified example files into the working directory.
    cp /lammps_src/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /app/ && \
    # Clean up the source code and build artifacts to minimize the final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /lammps_src

# mpirun --mca btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism none -np <cores> lmp -in <input_script>
# Setting a default command to the lammps executable.
CMD ["lmp"]

kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-mc
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 4 -v y 4 -v z 3 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    launcher: false
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge
  size: 1
  tasks: 48

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
#
# MiniCluster Manifest for a LAMMPS ReaxFF experiment
# API Version: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
# This manifest defines a Flux MiniCluster to run a specific HPC container
# on a single node in a Kubernetes cluster.
#
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster instance.
  name: lammps-reax-mc
  # Deployment will occur in the 'default' namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of MPI tasks to run within the MiniCluster. Flux will execute 'flux run -n 4 ...'
  tasks: 4

  # Do not delete the pods and other resources after the job completes.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs and results.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging configuration for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # If true, the operator will fail on any logging errors. This ensures robust log handling.
    strict: true

  # Define the container(s) that make up the MiniCluster.
  # In this case, a single container is used for the application.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command that will be wrapped by 'flux run'.
      # Flux Operator handles the 'flux run' prefix automatically.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # As instructed, this container is not a dedicated launcher.
      # The operator will use this as the lead broker and job submitter by default.
      launcher: false

This attempt targets a significant performance increase by selecting the hpc7g.16xlarge instance, which has the highest core count (64 Graviton3 cores) and is designed for HPC workloads. The configuration is updated to fully utilize this node by setting tasks to 64 and using an optimal 4x4x4 domain decomposition. This should provide a much stronger performance baseline.

The previous run on a 64-core ARM instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) yielded a strong FOM of 352.293. This attempt will test the best available x86 alternative, the 48-core c7a.12xlarge (AMD), to determine if architecture or single-core performance can further improve the FOM. The task count and domain decomposition are adjusted to fully utilize the 48 cores.

The peak FOM of 352.293 was achieved on the 64-core ARM-based hpc7g.16xlarge instance. The subsequent attempt on a 48-core AMD instance (c7a.12xlarge) resulted in a significantly lower FOM of 213.887. This indicates that for this specific LAMMPS workload, the higher core count and architecture of the Graviton3 HPC instance provide the best performance among the available options. Further attempts on instances with fewer cores or different specializations are unlikely to surpass this result.
